title: Umami
approach: Image Service plus a PostgreSQL Datastore on the same private network.
verify: Current Umami requires PostgreSQL and a runtime `DATABASE_URL`; do not use an older MySQL recipe.
description: Umami is a privacy-focused website analytics tool for tracking visits, pages, and events.

title: Grafana
approach: Adapt Grafana's upstream Compose setup, with persistent storage for `/var/lib/grafana`.
verify: Choose the current `grafana/grafana` OSS image and back up the Service volume separately.
description: Grafana helps teams explore metrics, logs, and other operational data through dashboards.

title: Gitea
approach: Adapt the upstream Compose project, preserving its persistent data volume.
verify: Preserve `/data`; web routing does not by itself expose Git-over-SSH.
description: Gitea is a lightweight Git hosting service for repositories, code reviews, and team collaboration.

title: Forgejo
approach: Adapt its upstream container installation to a Compose project.
verify: Preserve `/data` and plan SSH access separately from HTTP routing.
description: Forgejo is a self-hosted Git forge for code, issues, reviews, and collaboration.

title: Vaultwarden
approach: Adapt the upstream Compose setup with a persistent volume at `/data`.
verify: Set the public `DOMAIN` through a runtime value and verify TLS before creating accounts.
description: Vaultwarden is a lightweight server for Bitwarden-compatible password vaults.

title: Uptime Kuma
approach: Image Service with a named volume at `/app/data`.
verify: Use local storage with POSIX file locking; keep a separate copy of the Service volume.
description: Uptime Kuma monitors websites and services and displays their availability on status pages.

title: Metabase
approach: Adapt the upstream Compose setup with a PostgreSQL application database in the same Compose project.
verify: Configure the application database per upstream guidance; its embedded default is a quick start, not the production plan.
description: Metabase helps teams explore data, build dashboards, and share answers.

title: Paperless-ngx
approach: Adapt the upstream PostgreSQL Compose variant, including its own database service.
verify: Its Compose setup has multiple dependencies and persistent directories; replace unsupported bind mounts with permitted volumes or use another deployment method.
description: Paperless-ngx organizes scanned documents and PDFs into a searchable digital archive.

title: Meilisearch
approach: Adapt the upstream Compose setup with a persistent data volume.
verify: Set its production master key as a runtime secret and verify the image's data path and health endpoint for the chosen release.
description: Meilisearch adds fast, typo-tolerant search to applications.

title: Jellyfin
approach: Adapt the upstream container setup for HTTP streaming with persistent configuration, cache, and media storage.
verify: The HTTP app listens on port 8096. DLNA, host networking, and hardware transcoding need separate platform capabilities.
description: Jellyfin organizes and streams movies, shows, music, and other personal media.

title: Existing Dockerfile
approach: Use `deployment.type: dockerfile`, `context`, and `dockerfile`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/dockerfile)
verify: Deploy the committed Dockerfile and open its health endpoint. Confirm the deployment records the intended commit.

title: Multi-stage Dockerfile
approach: Add `deployment.target` to select the runtime stage. [Example](/docs/services/modes/dockerfile)
verify: Deploy the selected target stage and check its health endpoint. Confirm build tools are absent from the runtime image.

title: Private packages
approach: Declare `secrets.build` and mount it through BuildKit in a Dockerfile. [Secrets](/docs/secrets/towbar)
verify: Build with the declared secret and inspect the final image and generated assets for accidental credential inclusion.

title: Build server
approach: Set `buildServer` for a source-build Service. [Modes](/docs/platform-deployments)
verify: Check the deployment logs identify the selected builder and runtime servers, then verify the service on its runtime host.

title: Static site
approach: Use `deployment.type: static`, `buildCommand`, and `output`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/static)
verify: Open the deployed site and a static asset. Confirm the build produced the configured output directory.

title: Single-page app
approach: In static mode, set `spaFallback: true`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/static)
verify: Open a client-side route directly, then reload it. Both requests should load the application.

title: Railpack-detected project
approach: Use the pinned `railpack` version and frontend image from its guide. [Example](/docs/services/modes/railpack)
verify: Inspect the detected build and start command, then check the deployed health endpoint. Use Dockerfile mode if the build needs credentials.

title: Nixpacks project
approach: Use the pinned `nixpacks` builder and optional `configFile`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/nixpacks)
verify: Check the generated image starts and passes readiness. Use Dockerfile mode if the build needs credentials.

title: Buildpack project
approach: Pin `packImage` and a reviewed `builder`. [Example](/docs/services/modes/buildpack)
verify: Deploy with the reviewed builder digest and check the resulting process and readiness endpoint.

title: OCI image
approach: Run a reviewed OCI image with an explicit digest. [Image deployment](/docs/services/modes/image)
verify: Confirm the deployment records an immutable image digest and the image answers on the declared port.

title: HTTP API
approach: Set `container.port` and `health.path`. [Container and health](/docs/services/configuration)
verify: Call the health endpoint without a login. Confirm the process listens on the container interface rather than loopback.

title: Slow startup
approach: Increase `health.timeoutSeconds` only to a measured startup bound. [Container and health](/docs/services/configuration)
verify: Measure startup time from the deployment stages. Set the timeout above that bound and confirm promotion waits for readiness.

title: CPU-bound process
approach: Set `container.resources.cpus` and `memory`. [Container and health](/docs/services/configuration)
verify: Check CPU and memory during a representative load. For rolling replacement, leave memory headroom for the additional containers.

title: Private API
approach: Set `container.network` and omit public `domains`. [Private connectivity](/docs/services/configuration#private-connectivity)
verify: From a peer on the same host and network, resolve the API alias and call its endpoint.

title: PostgreSQL service
approach: Give both workloads `container.network: application`; use the Datastore alias and port in a secret URL. [PostgreSQL](/docs/databases/postgresql)
verify: After database readiness, query PostgreSQL from the service using its saved connection URL.

title: Redis service
approach: Share a private network and save an authenticated Redis URL as a runtime secret. [Redis](/docs/databases/redis)
verify: Connect from the service using the saved Redis password and perform an application-level read and write.

title: Persistent files
approach: Add a named `container.volumes` mount and a `recreate` rollout. [Storage](/docs/services/configuration#persistent-storage)
verify: Write a test file as the application user, redeploy, and confirm the file remains readable.

title: Public HTTPS
approach: Set `domains.primary` and a supported `tls.mode`. [Routing and TLS](/docs/services/routing)
verify: Open the HTTPS hostname and inspect its certificate and application response after deployment.

title: Alternate domain
approach: Add a domain alias according to [routing](/docs/services/routing).
verify: Request both hostnames and confirm each serves the intended service or configured redirect.

title: Single-writer data
approach: Use `rollout.type: recreate` with `maintenanceMode: true` and a reason. [Storage](/docs/services/configuration#persistent-storage)
verify: Inspect replacement stages to confirm the old writer stops before the new one starts. Verify existing files afterward.

title: Runtime credential
approach: List its key under `secrets.runtime`, then save the value in **Settings → Secrets**. [Towbar secrets](/docs/secrets/towbar)
verify: Save the declared value in the selected environment, deploy, and confirm the application can use it without logging it.

title: Build dependency
approach: Declare a build-stage key and use a Dockerfile BuildKit secret mount. [Towbar secrets](/docs/secrets/towbar)
verify: Inspect the build result and final image for accidental credential inclusion. Keep the value out of committed files.

title: Infisical folder
approach: Set `externalSecrets.integration: infisical`, project, and optional `environmentSlug` or `secretPath`. [External secrets](/docs/secrets/external)
verify: Deploy using the selected Infisical folder and confirm the application receives every required runtime key.

title: Doppler config
approach: Set `externalSecrets.integration: doppler`, project, and optional config. [External secrets](/docs/secrets/external)
verify: Deploy using the selected Doppler config and confirm the application can use its required runtime values.

title: Monorepo auto-deploy
approach: List relevant paths in `autoDeploy.inputs`. [Automation](/docs/services/automation)
verify: Push a relevant application change and a shared dependency change. Confirm each queues deployment; an unrelated change should not.

title: Pull-request preview
approach: Enable previews in root `towbar.yml`, then set the Service `preview` block. [Previews](/docs/previews)
verify: Open an eligible pull request, wait for preview deployment, and check its URL. Verify it uses isolated preview credentials.

title: Daily report
approach: Add a `jobs` entry with an argument-array command and five-field cron. [Jobs](/docs/services/jobs)
verify: Run the job manually, inspect its output and final state, then verify the next scheduled run appears.

title: Pre-deploy migration
approach: Use a pre-deploy hook and stage-specific secrets. [Deployment hooks](/docs/deployments#deployment-hooks)
verify: Run the migration against test data, verify the schema, and check compatibility with the previous application release.

title: Event notifications
approach: Add `notifications` to select workspace-configured destinations. [Notifications](/docs/integrations/notifications)
verify: Trigger a test event and inspect delivery history. Confirm the configured destination receives it.

title: Vulnerability scanning
approach: Set `vulnerabilityScanning` and review the result before release. [Scanning](/docs/vulnerability-scanning)
verify: Inspect the completed scan for the deployed image digest and review its package findings and fixed versions.

title: Single-service PostgreSQL
approach: Set `type: postgres`, a private network, and the required `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`.
verify: Query PostgreSQL from the service using the private alias on port 5432 and its saved connection URL.

title: Named PostgreSQL
approach: Declare `POSTGRES_USER` and `POSTGRES_DB` alongside the password.
verify: After first initialization, connect and check the configured database and role exist. Later changes require SQL, not just new secret values.

title: PostgreSQL tunnel
approach: Add `access.sshTunnel.hostPort` to the Datastore.
verify: Forward the loopback-bound database port over SSH and connect with a local PostgreSQL client.

title: PostgreSQL backups
approach: Add a [backup policy](/docs/backups) with an enabled provider, daily cron, and retention.
verify: Create a backup, check restore-readiness, then perform a restore drill with disposable data.

title: MySQL API
approach: Use `type: mysql`, a private network, and `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`.
verify: Connect from the application on port 3306 using its application user rather than the datastore root credential.

title: MySQL schema
approach: Declare `MYSQL_DATABASE`, `MYSQL_USER`, and `MYSQL_PASSWORD` before first deployment.
verify: Connect as the application user and check it can access the configured MySQL database.

title: MySQL copies
approach: Add a backup destination and retention policy.
verify: Create a backup, inspect its saved object, and complete a restore drill with disposable data.

title: MariaDB CMS
approach: Use `type: mariadb`, private networking, and `MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD`.
verify: Run the CMS initialization and a representative read/write against the selected MariaDB version.

title: MariaDB role
approach: Declare `MYSQL_DATABASE`, `MYSQL_USER`, and `MYSQL_PASSWORD` at creation.
verify: Connect as the application user and check its privileges. Rotate existing users with SQL before updating saved credentials.

title: MariaDB tunnel
approach: Add a loopback-only SSH tunnel port and keep regular app traffic private.
verify: Connect through the SSH-forwarded port. Confirm port 3306 remains unavailable to public clients.

title: MongoDB API
approach: Use `type: mongodb` and the same `container.network` as the API.
verify: Connect from the API through the MongoDB alias on port 27017 and query the intended database.

title: MongoDB initialization
approach: Declare `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME` and `MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD`.
verify: Deploy to an empty volume, then authenticate with the configured root user against the admin database.

title: MongoDB user
approach: Create a least-privilege database user after initialization.
verify: Query from the service using the application user and verify it lacks administrative privileges.

title: MongoDB access
approach: Add `access.sshTunnel.hostPort` without public database routing.
verify: Connect a MongoDB client through SSH using the intended authentication database.

title: MongoDB recovery
approach: Schedule a provider-backed backup and practice a fresh-target restore.
verify: Restore disposable data, then query it with an application client after the operation completes.

title: ClickHouse analytics
approach: Use `type: clickhouse` on the analytics Service's private network.
verify: Send an authenticated query from the service to the ClickHouse alias on HTTP port 8123.

title: ClickHouse credentials
approach: Declare `CLICKHOUSE_USER` and `CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD`.
verify: Save the values in the selected environment, deploy, and test an authenticated ClickHouse query.

title: ClickHouse selection
approach: Optionally declare `CLICKHOUSE_DB` before initial deployment.
verify: Query the configured database and confirm the consuming service selects it.

title: ClickHouse sizing
approach: Set `container.resources` for measured ingest and query load.
verify: Run representative ingestion and queries, then inspect CPU, memory, and disk growth before choosing production limits.

title: ClickHouse recovery
approach: Add a supported backup provider and test a fresh-target archive restore.
verify: Complete a restore drill and query representative data from the restored ClickHouse datastore.

title: Redis sessions
approach: Use `type: redis`, a private network, and `REDIS_PASSWORD`.
verify: Create and retrieve a session through the application using its authenticated Redis connection.

title: Redis queue
approach: Give the producer and worker the same private network and secret URL.
verify: Enqueue and process a test job. Restart the client and verify reconnection and the intended key prefix.

title: Redis tunnel
approach: Add `access.sshTunnel.hostPort`.
verify: Forward the loopback-bound cache port over SSH and run an authenticated client command.

title: Redis recovery
approach: Run a backup and verify a fresh-target RDB restore.
verify: After a restore drill, query the dataset and confirm append-only persistence resumes.

title: Dragonfly client
approach: Use `type: dragonfly` and `REDIS_PASSWORD`.
verify: Run the application or queue library's actual Redis-protocol commands against Dragonfly, beyond a connection check.

title: Dragonfly endpoint
approach: Share `container.network` with the consuming Service.
verify: From the service, authenticate to the Dragonfly alias on port 6379 and read/write a test key.

title: Dragonfly recovery
approach: Test a verified snapshot and a same-engine restore.
verify: Complete a restore drill, then query the restored Dragonfly dataset through its client.

title: KeyDB amd64
approach: Use `type: keydb` and `REDIS_PASSWORD`.
verify: Choose an amd64 server, deploy, and verify an authenticated client command. The reviewed KeyDB image does not support arm64.

title: KeyDB endpoint
approach: Share a network with the consuming Service and keep the port private.
verify: Use an authenticated client on the private network to read/write a test key on port 6379.

title: KeyDB recovery
approach: Back up and restore into a fresh KeyDB target.
verify: Restore a backup from the same KeyDB major version, then verify the dataset on an amd64 target.

title: Manual backup
approach: Configure an enabled storage provider and choose **Back up now**.
verify: Run a manual backup and inspect its final result, storage object, and restore-readiness.

title: Daily retention
approach: Add `backup.schedule` with UTC cron and `retention.keepLast`.
verify: Check the next scheduled run completes. After exceeding keepLast, confirm retention removes older copies.

title: AWS S3
approach: Use `backup.integration: aws` with the runtime AWS provider enabled.
verify: Create a backup and restore drill in the selected bucket and prefix. Check retention can delete expired objects.

title: S3-compatible destination
approach: Select an enabled `s3` or `r2` provider as appropriate.
verify: Create and inspect a backup using the configured endpoint, bucket, encryption settings, and credentials.

title: Google Cloud
approach: Select an enabled `gcs` provider.
verify: Create a backup in the designated bucket and verify a restore drill using the configured Google Cloud identity.

title: Cloud copies
approach: Declare both `s3` and `gcs` destinations and set `restoreFrom`.
verify: Inspect both stored copies and their assurance results. Run a restore drill using the selected authoritative provider.

title: Restore drill
approach: Restore a known recovery point into a fresh target.
verify: Restore disposable data, wait for the final result, then query representative records through an application client.

title: Server placement
approach: Override the Datastore's server in another environment.
verify: Deploy on the selected environment's server and verify authenticated connectivity with that environment's secrets.

title: Password rotation
approach: Change the user inside the database first, then update Towbar's saved value.
verify: After rotation, test database login, the application connection, and a backup using the new credential.

title: Incident investigation
approach: Inspect recovery-point freshness and operation events.
verify: Inspect freshness separately from object-readiness errors. Follow the failed check before retrying backup or restore.

title: PostgreSQL stack
approach: Dockerfile Service + scoped PostgreSQL Datastore; the secret URL uses the Datastore's declared network alias on port 5432. [PostgreSQL](/docs/databases/postgresql)
verify: Query PostgreSQL from the application using a role with only the required privileges.

title: MySQL stack
approach: Dockerfile Service + scoped MySQL Datastore; the secret URL uses the Datastore's declared network alias on port 3306. [MySQL](/docs/databases/mysql)
verify: Run an application read/write against MySQL 8.4 and confirm its schema initialization succeeds.

title: MariaDB stack
approach: CMS Service + `mariadb` Datastore; share a network and use an app user. [MariaDB](/docs/databases/mariadb)
verify: Initialize the CMS against MariaDB, then create and retrieve a test record.

title: MongoDB stack
approach: API Service + `mongodb` Datastore; create an app user apart from Towbar's root user. [MongoDB](/docs/databases/mongodb)
verify: Query MongoDB from the application using the intended user and authentication database.

title: Session stack
approach: Web Service + `redis` Datastore; use a secret authenticated URL. [Redis](/docs/databases/redis)
verify: Create a session, restart Redis in a test environment, and check the application's expected session behavior.

title: Dragonfly queue
approach: Producer Service + worker Service + `dragonfly` Datastore. [Dragonfly](/docs/databases/dragonfly)
verify: Enqueue and process a job with the actual queue library, then verify reconnection behavior.

title: Search-backed API
approach: API Service with `SEARCH_URL` and `SEARCH_KEY` for an existing Meilisearch endpoint. [Meilisearch upstream](https://www.meilisearch.com/integrations/docker)
verify: Index and search a test document through the API. Keep the Meilisearch master key in runtime secrets and back up its volume separately.

title: Event analytics
approach: Ingest Service + `clickhouse` Datastore on one private network. [ClickHouse](/docs/databases/clickhouse)
verify: Ingest and query representative events, then measure disk growth and query resource use.

title: Internal Metabase
approach: Metabase and its PostgreSQL application database in one adapted Compose project. [Metabase upstream](https://www.metabase.com/docs/latest/installation-and-operation/running-metabase-on-docker)
verify: Complete Metabase setup with its PostgreSQL application database. Confirm settings survive a project redeployment.

title: Umami analytics
approach: Umami image Service + `postgres` Datastore; `DATABASE_URL` is a runtime secret. [Umami upstream](https://docs.umami.is/docs/install)
verify: Sign in, change the initial administrator password, and confirm a test site records a pageview.

title: API-worker stack
approach: Deploy `redis`, then private API and worker Services on its network.
verify: Submit a job through the API, confirm the worker processes it, and test client reconnection.

title: Daily reports
approach: Declare a [job](/docs/services/jobs) on the API's deployed image.
verify: Run the report manually, inspect bounded output, and verify a repeat run does not duplicate its effects.

title: Webhook worker
approach: Keep the receiver public, worker private, and share a cache or database on one server.
verify: Send a test webhook and confirm worker processing. Verify the worker has no public route.

title: Frontend API
approach: Deploy a static Service and a separately routed API Service.
verify: Open the frontend and confirm browser requests reach the HTTPS API. Browser clients cannot resolve private Docker aliases.

title: Multi-process repository
approach: Use a `.compose.yml` project when components must be deployed together. [Compose](/docs/services/modes/compose)
verify: Inspect the resolved Compose project, deploy it, and verify every required service is healthy.

title: Web previews
approach: Enable root environment previews and Service preview settings. [Previews](/docs/previews)
verify: Open an eligible pull request and verify its preview with isolated secrets. Connect explicitly to a disposable database if needed.

title: Staging production
approach: Map each environment to its branch and server. [Environment branches](/docs/repositories/environments)
verify: Deploy both environments and confirm each uses its own hostname, credentials, server, and resource limits.

title: Stateful web
approach: Use a single-writer Service volume with `recreate` rollout plus a Datastore.
verify: Write a test upload, redeploy, and verify it persists. Test the separate backup process for the service volume.

title: Shared database
approach: Deploy the database, save a separate URL in each Service, then deploy them.
verify: Query from both services using their own least-privilege database roles and check connection limits under representative load.

title: Isolated stacks
approach: Place each Service and its Datastore on one server, with a second independent pair on another server.
verify: Query each datastore from its local service. Docker networks with the same name on different servers do not connect the hosts.

title: Plausible CE
approach: Adapt Plausible Community Edition with PostgreSQL and ClickHouse on one server.
verify: Keep both database volumes private and persistent; route only Plausible HTTP through Towbar.
setup: Set the public BASE_URL and generate a unique SECRET_KEY_BASE. Keep PostgreSQL and ClickHouse credentials outside Git.
description: Plausible Community Edition is a privacy-focused website analytics platform.

title: Matomo
approach: Adapt the official Compose setup with MariaDB and a report-archiving cron container.
verify: Verify the archive job runs and preserve both Matomo files and the MariaDB volume.
setup: Use unique MariaDB credentials and replace upstream host ports with Towbar ingress. Keep the archiving container in the Compose project.
description: Matomo tracks website and app usage through visitor reports and goals.

title: GlitchTip
approach: Adapt GlitchTip’s Compose setup with PostgreSQL and optional Valkey.
verify: Check the public domain, background processing, email delivery, and persistent uploads.
setup: Set GLITCHTIP_DOMAIN, SECRET_KEY, and email configuration. Keep the PostgreSQL and upload volumes persistent.
description: GlitchTip helps teams track application errors, performance, and uptime.

title: Prometheus
approach: Run Prometheus with a versioned scrape configuration and persistent metrics volume.
verify: Verify the intended targets are scraped; do not expose internal metrics or the admin API publicly by accident.
setup: Bake prometheus.yml into a custom image because Towbar Compose does not accept host bind mounts. Persist /prometheus with a named volume.
description: Prometheus collects and queries metrics from applications and infrastructure.

title: VictoriaMetrics
approach: Run single-node VictoriaMetrics with a persistent data volume.
verify: Confirm ingestion and retention settings before using it as a metrics store.
setup: Persist /victoria-metrics-data in a Docker-managed volume and keep the write endpoint private unless callers need public access.
description: VictoriaMetrics stores and queries metrics for monitoring and analysis.

title: Gatus
approach: Run Gatus with a versioned endpoint configuration.
verify: Check that endpoint checks execute and notifications reach the intended destination.
setup: Bake the Gatus configuration into the image or use a supported volume; Towbar Compose does not accept host bind mounts.
description: Gatus checks service endpoints and displays their health on a status page.

title: Keycloak
approach: Run Keycloak with PostgreSQL and an HTTPS public hostname.
verify: Use the production start mode rather than start-dev, and verify the external hostname and login flow.
setup: Build an optimized image, set KC_DB to postgres, and supply the database and bootstrap admin credentials securely.
description: Keycloak provides sign-in and single sign-on for applications.

title: authentik
approach: Adapt authentik’s official Compose stack with PostgreSQL and its worker.
verify: Verify initial setup and preserve the database, media, and certificate data.
setup: Set a unique secret key and PostgreSQL password; route the server’s HTTP port through Towbar without publishing host ports.
description: authentik manages users, sign-in, and single sign-on across applications.

title: Ghost
approach: Adapt the official Ghost Docker project with its MySQL database.
verify: Verify the canonical URL, uploads, database persistence, and mail configuration.
setup: Remove the bundled public reverse proxy when Towbar provides ingress, and keep Ghost’s database and content volumes persistent.
description: Ghost is a publishing platform for websites, newsletters, and memberships.

title: WordPress
approach: Run WordPress with a private MySQL or MariaDB database.
verify: Preserve wp-content and database data; check uploads and plugin updates after deployment.
setup: Use unique database credentials and keep the database service private in the same Compose project.
description: WordPress is a content management system for websites and blogs.

title: Wiki.js
approach: Run Wiki.js with a PostgreSQL database.
verify: Verify the database connection and preserve the PostgreSQL volume before importing content.
setup: Set DB_TYPE to postgres and point Wiki.js to the private database service name.
description: Wiki.js helps teams create and maintain documentation and knowledge bases.

title: Navidrome
approach: Run Navidrome with separate data and music volumes.
verify: Confirm the music library is readable and back up the database stored under /data.
setup: Persist /data and make the music library available at /music through a Docker-managed volume; Towbar Compose does not accept host bind mounts.
description: Navidrome streams a personal music library through a web player and compatible apps.

title: Node-RED
approach: Run Node-RED with a persistent flow data volume.
verify: Verify flows survive replacement and protect the editor before exposing it publicly.
setup: Persist /data with a named volume and set a unique credential secret for encrypted flow credentials.
description: Node-RED lets you connect services and devices through automation flows in a visual editor.

title: Typesense
approach: Run Typesense with a persistent search index and an API key.
verify: Verify the collection survives replacement and the API key is not embedded in public clients.
setup: Persist /data and supply a strong API key through the protected runtime configuration.
description: Typesense is a search engine for building fast search experiences in applications.

title: SearXNG
approach: Adapt SearXNG’s container setup with its configuration and optional Valkey.
verify: Verify search works and the public instance has appropriate rate limits.
setup: Bake settings.yml into an image or use a supported volume; remove public host ports from the upstream Compose file.
description: SearXNG combines results from multiple search engines in a self-hosted search interface.

title: FreshRSS
approach: Run FreshRSS with persistent data and extension volumes.
verify: Confirm feeds refresh on schedule and the database survives container replacement.
setup: Persist /var/www/FreshRSS/data and /var/www/FreshRSS/extensions in named volumes; configure the refresh schedule.
description: FreshRSS gathers updates from websites and feeds into one reading app.

title: linkding
approach: Run linkding with a persistent bookmark database.
verify: Create an initial admin account and confirm bookmarks survive a redeployment.
setup: Persist /etc/linkding/data with a named volume and configure trusted origins for the public domain if needed.
description: linkding saves and organizes web bookmarks in a simple self-hosted library.

title: HedgeDoc
approach: Adapt HedgeDoc’s Compose example with PostgreSQL and upload storage.
verify: Set the public domain and preserve both the database and uploaded files.
setup: Replace example database passwords, set CMD_DOMAIN for the public hostname, and keep the database and uploads on named volumes.
description: HedgeDoc lets people write and edit Markdown notes together in real time.

title: Huginn
approach: Adapt Huginn’s Docker setup with MySQL.
verify: Change the initial admin password and confirm agents execute after the service starts.
setup: Use the official single-process image layout and adapt unsupported legacy Compose fields such as volumes_from to named volumes.
description: Huginn runs agents that watch events online and trigger automated actions.

title: ChangeDetection.io
approach: Run ChangeDetection.io with a persistent watch datastore.
verify: Confirm saved watches survive replacement; add a browser sidecar only if JavaScript pages need it.
setup: Persist /datastore with a named volume and remove upstream host port publishing when routing through Towbar.
description: ChangeDetection.io watches web pages and alerts you when their content changes.

title: Nextcloud
approach: Adapt the Apache-image Compose example with MariaDB and persistent data.
verify: Confirm uploads, background jobs, and database backups before inviting users.
setup: Use the Apache image for port 80, preserve its application volume and the MariaDB volume, and set trusted domains and reverse-proxy settings for the public hostname.
description: Nextcloud gives teams a place to store, sync, and share files.

title: Immich
approach: Adapt Immich's current Compose file with its PostgreSQL and machine-learning services.
verify: Back up both uploads and PostgreSQL data; confirm thumbnail and search jobs finish.
setup: Keep the upstream service layout and required database extensions. Replace bind-mounted upload and database paths with supported persistent storage before syncing.
description: Immich backs up, organizes, and browses photos and videos from your devices.

title: BookStack
approach: Run the LinuxServer BookStack image with a private MariaDB service.
verify: Check the public URL, first login, attachments, and database recovery.
setup: Set APP_URL and a generated APP_KEY, save database credentials outside Git, and persist /config and the MariaDB data directory.
description: BookStack organizes documentation into books, chapters, and pages for teams.

title: Calibre-Web
approach: Run Calibre-Web with separate configuration and book-library volumes.
verify: Confirm the configured Calibre library is readable and its database survives replacement.
setup: Persist /config and provide a prepared Calibre library at /books using supported volumes. Do not assume an empty /books volume contains a library.
description: Calibre-Web lets you browse and read books from an existing Calibre library.

title: PhotoPrism
approach: Adapt PhotoPrism's Compose example with MariaDB and persistent originals.
verify: Index a small album, check originals and storage persist, and test the database backup.
setup: Set a unique initial admin password before first start. Keep originals, application storage, and MariaDB data on persistent volumes.
description: PhotoPrism organizes and searches a personal photo collection.

title: Miniflux
approach: Run Miniflux with PostgreSQL for feed and account data.
verify: Add a feed, confirm scheduled refreshes, and restore from a database backup.
setup: Set DATABASE_URL to the private PostgreSQL service and configure the initial administrator securely. Keep the database volume persistent.
description: Miniflux is a minimal feed reader for following articles from websites you choose.

title: ntfy
approach: Run ntfy with a persistent message cache and explicit access policy.
verify: Publish and receive a test message, then verify unauthenticated access matches the intended policy.
setup: Run the image with the serve command, persist /var/cache/ntfy, and provide a versioned server configuration without a host bind mount. Configure authentication before exposing private topics.
description: ntfy sends and receives notifications through topics you can subscribe to.

title: Jenkins
approach: Run the Jenkins LTS controller with persistent home data and separately managed build agents.
verify: Complete the setup wizard, test an agent connection, and back up Jenkins home.
setup: Persist /var/jenkins_home. The controller image does not include a Docker CLI; plan build agents separately and do not mount the host Docker socket into this Compose project.
description: Jenkins automates software builds, tests, and delivery pipelines.

title: Vikunja
approach: Run one Vikunja Service with persistent SQLite and uploaded files for a small first instance.
verify: Create a project and upload a file; verify both survive redeployment.
description: Vikunja is a task and project manager for organizing work across teams.

title: Kanboard
approach: Run the official image with persistent SQLite data and a separate plugins volume.
verify: Change the initial administrator password, create a board, and verify it survives redeployment.
description: Kanboard is a Kanban board for planning and tracking project tasks.

title: Excalidraw
approach: Run the official client image; self-hosted collaboration and sharing require additional upstream services.
verify: Draw and export a diagram; confirm the limitations before treating it as a shared workspace.
description: Excalidraw is a browser-based whiteboard for sketches and diagrams.

title: Memos
approach: Run Memos with its SQLite data on a persistent Service volume.
verify: Create a note and verify it survives redeployment.
description: Memos is a lightweight place to capture and share short notes.

title: Gotify
approach: Run Gotify with persistent SQLite storage and a protected initial administrator account.
verify: Send a test message and confirm the account and message survive redeployment.
description: Gotify receives application messages and delivers them to its web and mobile clients.

title: File Browser
approach: Run File Browser with separate persistent file, database, and configuration volumes.
verify: Retrieve the initial administrator password from logs, upload a file, and verify it survives redeployment.
description: File Browser gives you a web interface to browse, upload, and manage files.

title: Actual Budget
approach: Run Actual with its server data on a persistent volume and HTTPS for browser access.
verify: Create a budget and confirm it remains after redeployment.
description: Actual Budget helps you plan spending and track personal finances.

title: Audiobookshelf
approach: Run Audiobookshelf with persistent configuration, metadata, and media volumes.
verify: Import an audiobook, play it, and verify the library remains after redeployment.
description: Audiobookshelf organizes and streams audiobooks and podcasts.

title: Stirling PDF
approach: Run the official image with persistent configuration and change its initial administrator password.
verify: Process a test PDF and verify the settings survive redeployment.
description: Stirling PDF offers browser-based tools for editing and converting PDF files.

title: CyberChef
approach: Run the official prebuilt web image; it needs no database or persistent server volume.
verify: Open the page and test an encoding operation.
description: CyberChef is a browser-based toolkit for encoding, decoding, and transforming data.

title: IT-Tools
approach: Run the official web image; this first deployment needs no database or persistent volume.
verify: Open the page and try a conversion tool.
description: IT-Tools brings common developer and IT utilities into one browser interface.

title: Ollama
approach: Run the CPU image privately with a persistent model volume; model downloads and hardware capacity are separate steps.
verify: Pull a small model and verify the private API lists it after redeployment.
description: Ollama serves downloadable AI models through a local API.

title: LocalAI
approach: Run the CPU image privately with persistent models, backends, configuration, and data volumes.
verify: Install a small compatible model and query it through the private API.
description: LocalAI runs AI models locally behind an API compatible with common model clients.

title: Copyparty
approach: Run the official image privately with persistent shared files and configuration; its default share is writable.
verify: Upload and download a test file over a trusted connection before configuring public access.
description: Copyparty is a web-based file server for sharing, browsing, and uploading files.
